subject: Money
title: Debt Deflation Spiral
description: A 60-second lesson on Debt Deflation Spiral.

hook.text: Economist Irving Fisher lost his fortune in the 1929 crash. Then he explained exactly why deflation kills economies.

buildup.text: Fisher's theory: when prices fall, debt's real burden increases. Borrowers sell assets to pay debts.

discovery.text: Mass selling drives prices down further, making remaining debt even heavier. A self-reinforcing doom loop.

twist.text: In 2008, U.S. home prices fell 30%. Homeowners owed more than their houses were worth—negative equity.

climax.text: Debt deflation turns individual losses into systemic collapse. One person's firesale becomes everyone's crisis.

quiz.question: What is the debt deflation spiral?
options: Falling prices increasing debt burden, causing more selling and further price drops
